text:
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for `prompt-shard` -> routing 5% traffic to canary. Canary ID: canary-ptshard-20240308. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/ptshard

Mia (oncall): saw the page. joining. link?

deploy-bot: Alert: canary-ptshard-20240308 5xx rate spiked from 0.3% -> 12.6% in 2min. Error signature: "kv_cache_key_error". Triggering emergency page for `incidents` oncall.

Noah (eng-runtime): I pushed the canary ~2m ago. logs show: `RuntimeError: KV cache failed to attach; fallback path raised OOM` repeatedly for requests > seq 512. guessing quant kernel mismatch with new compilation profile.

Olivia (prod-sre): getting customer reports: 3 high-priority timeouts from enterprise tenants (ACME Inc, BetaApps). CS-Leah, are we seeing escalations?

CS-Leah: yes, CS already filed tickets. customers seeing partial timeouts and degraded completions. Preparing a quick note.

Mia (oncall): we don't need to wait. activating emergency feature-flag kill-switch for prompt routing to remove canary traffic. Executing: `./ffctl toggle --feature prompt_shard_routing --value false --reason "canary 5xx spike"`

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: `prompt_shard_routing=false` by Mia. 5% canary traffic routed back to stable.

Noah (eng-runtime): confirmed: within 20s the error rate started to fall. instrumented logs show canary->stable routing change applied.

Olivia (prod-sre): metrics: 5xx rate dropped to baseline 0.4% after ~48s. Latency back to normal. :white_check_mark:

Mia (oncall): good. I'll keep the page open for 30m and then hand off to Olivia for 1hr watch. Noah, can you start a rollback of the canary artifact in CI and capture the build args?

Noah (eng-runtime): Rolling back canary tag: `ci rollback canary-ptshard-20240308 --to tag=ptshard-v1`

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued: job-7892. Estimated completion 2m.

Noah (eng-runtime): rollback completed. New traffic graph shows stable route only. attaching brief log snippet:
```
2024-03-08T14:02:31Z INFO route set stable
2024-03-08T14:02:59Z INFO canary teardown successful
```

CS-Leah: I'll send the customer note: "We observed a degraded experience this morning tied to an experimental routing rollout. We've reverted the change and are monitoring; CS will follow up with impacted customers." Do you want me to include any technical details?

Olivia (prod-sre): keep it high level for customers. We'll put fuller RCA in the postmortem. Link to runbook used: https://runbooks.redwood.example/incident/ff-kill

Alex (PM): filing an incident ticket and scheduling a postmortem. Please add timeline + logs. INC-2024-0312-ptshard created.

Mia (oncall): handing off monitoring to Olivia at +30m. I'll remove myself from page then. Everyone add any notes to the incident ticket.

Olivia (prod-sre): taking watch. I'll coordinate with CS-Leah if we need to proactively notify more customers.

Noah (eng-runtime): quick note: stack trace shows kernel selector chose an AVX2-quant path that is incompatible with the new kv-cache layout under long sequences. Investigating compilation flags. Will put a safe-guard in deploy pipeline to block this profile until validated.

Mia (oncall): thanks. marking page resolved for oncall. Please escalate in ticket if we see a resurgence. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Page resolved by Mia (oncall). Duration: 00:12:15.

Alex (PM): thanks all — good quick reaction. We'll schedule a blameless postmortem and a checklist item to add explicit canary test for seq>512.

CS-Leah: customer notes sent to impacted accounts. I'll share responses in the incident ticket.

Olivia (prod-sre): monitoring until 15:10 UTC, then close if stable.

Mia (oncall): closing my oncall handoff. followup tasks: add canary test, tighten ff rollout policy, review kernel selector.

Noah (eng-runtime): filing a PR with a gating test now.

Olivia (prod-sre): thanks, team.
